statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-119375 is an information disclosure in SQLite's WAL reader: when a WAL file's page size is smaller than the database's, the page read from it is not fully initialized, so a crafted database and WAL file can make queries such as substr() return stale page-cache bytes, including other rows and internal pointers. SQLite lists it as fixed in 3.54.0: https://sqlite.org/cves.html, https://sqlite.org/src/info/f9b4ee369557c36c. The trunk fix is that check-in, mirrored as https://github.com/sqlite/sqlite/commit/e5bf119821f25be1d7f10ef0a2edbe175289166e, and the same change on the 3.53 maintenance branch is https://github.com/sqlite/sqlite/commit/cff880190d523dbfa0b3989e2ae268d2127800ef, which makes sqlite3WalReadFrame() in src/wal.c zero the rest of the page buffer with memset() when the WAL page size is the smaller one; it was committed after the 3.53.4 release. DHI's 3.53.4-r1 build is SQLite 3.53.4 with a backport of the branch commit. The DHI Alpine 3.23 package repository publishes packages built from source sqlite (sqlite, sqlite-libs, sqlite-static, sqlite-dev and sqlite-doc) at 3.51.1-r0, 3.51.2-r0, 3.53.4-r0 and 3.53.4-r1, for x86_64 and aarch64. We unpacked the sqlite, sqlite-libs, sqlite-static and sqlite-dev packages of every one of those builds on both architectures, each checked against its index checksum. SQLite is compiled into three files in each build: the sqlite3 shell in the sqlite package, which carries its own copy and does not link libsqlite3; the shared library in sqlite-libs; and the static archive libsqlite3.a in sqlite-static. sqlite-dev holds only headers, a pkg-config file and the libsqlite3.so link. The shell and both libraries report SQLite 3.51.1, 3.51.2, 3.53.4 and 3.53.4 in those builds. The 3.51.1-r0, 3.51.2-r0 and 3.53.4-r0 builds are built from the upstream 3.51.1, 3.51.2 and 3.53.4 releases, none of which contains the fix. The shared library and the shell are stripped, so we compared the compiled code of the static archive libsqlite3.a, which keeps its function names, in every build on x86_64 and aarch64: readDbPage(), into which the WAL frame read is inlined, calls memset() in 3.53.4-r1 and makes no memset() call in 3.51.1-r0, 3.51.2-r0 and 3.53.4-r0, on both architectures. The shell and the shared library in 3.53.4-r1 are built from the same patched source, and the reproducible fixes in the same build (for example CVE-2026-119371) behave as fixed in all three copies. So 3.51.1-r0, 3.51.2-r0 and 3.53.4-r0 are affected and 3.53.4-r1 is fixed.
